description: System-level canonical layout for the stroke-order tail. Every character's tail-spec MUST reference this anchor table — the mizige (米字格) position, size, and child-hand entry direction are NOT content design, they are process constraints. Without this table, every character drifts and the final frame stops being a coherent product surface (P03 poster).

frame.description: Recognition-video composition canvas. All anchor coordinates below are in this coordinate space.

background.description: Xuan paper warm cream. Same value used in cinematic body's ink-glyph plate so the cross-over into the tail does not flash.

mizige.description: Single mizige centered on the frame. recognition (0.18) is the state during the cinematic body when the glyph is being READ; writing (0.30) is the state during stroke-order tail when the glyph is being WRITTEN. Container policy is single-mizige-dual-state — never two grids on screen.

glyph.description: Kaiti glyph centers inside the mizige with ~30px breathing room. boxSize is the safe area for the character — strokes must not visually exceed this box even if the SVG viewBox is larger.

hand.description: A pointer enters from the bottom-right corner at 30°, its tip hovering ~18px above the LAST written stroke. The pointer form is allowed to be a child's right hand, a calligraphy brush, OR an ink-front bloom (a warm radial bloom that visually IS the ink advancing front) — the constraint is the entry direction, the tip position, and the 'guide-toward-stroke' semantic, NOT a specific anatomical depiction. v8.2 added brush-pointer after the cartoon hand SVG read as 'color blocks'. v9 added ink-front-bloom after jury found that even brush-pointer felt like a static prop disconnected from the writing act — ink-front-bloom collapses the pointer and the ink itself into one entity, so the bloom moves WITH the mask front by construction. Brand's P03 poster is still locked to bottom-right 30° entry and tip at glyph-right-end +18px.

lighting.description: Warm 30° rim light from top-right casts a soft shadow under the hand toward bottom-left. Locks all stroke-order tail final frames to one consistent lighting setup so the P03 poster reads coherently across the whole Unit-01 set.

timing.description: Stroke-order tail occupies the last 10.0-12.0s of a 12s recognition video. 0.0-0.6s: mizige opacity 0.18→0.30 and ink-glyph layer from the cinematic body MUST be cleared in this window (otherwise the previous renge ink leaks into the writing demo and the final frame shows ghost strokes). 0.6-1.5s: writing the strokes. 1.5-2.0s: final hold = poster moment.

clearingContract.description: When the stroke-order tail starts (t = totalDurationSeconds_before_tail), these cinematic-body layers MUST be removed from the DOM or set to opacity:0 with display:none. Failing this contract is what produced the 'two horizontal strokes' bug in v5 — the ink-glyph layer was still painted underneath the fresh stroke-order mask.

hook.description: Composite stroke — animator must split into a primary stroke + a short curve at the end.

turning.description: Composite stroke — animator must split into two linear phases joined at the turn.

domProbe.description: render-stroke-order-tail.mjs runs a Playwright DOM probe on the final frame and asserts: (a) tail container has data-tail-state=writing, (b) cinematic-body layers are marked removed. This is the only way to catch the 'ghost ink under final stroke' bug from screenshot review alone.
